findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed_category setting exists
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` returns no rows when `embed_category` was never set, which is the default state and the case on fresh installs. `[0]` is then nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, so the migration fails. The fallback `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15 has the same unguarded `[0]['value']`. The result must be checked before indexing.

findings.title: Unescaped setting value interpolated into raw INSERT SQL
findings.body: Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated directly as `'#{h}'`. A value containing a quote, or stray whitespace or a trailing `\r` from the multi-line setting, breaks the statement or can inject SQL. Values are also inserted without the trimming or normalization that the model's `before_validation` would apply. Use `connection.quote` or the model.

findings.title: before_validation raises on nil host and mutates in place
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil. The admin controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, so a missing host param gives a 500 instead of a validation error. `sub!` also mutates the attribute string in place, which bypasses dirty tracking. Use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`, guarded for nil.

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the input side and ignores ports
findings.body: The query compares `lower(host) = ?` against `uri.host`, which is not downcased, so a referer like `http://EviLTrout.com` never matches. The validation regex allows `host:port`, and `before_validation` keeps the port. `uri.host` never includes the port, so a host saved with a port can never match and is silently useless. Downcase the input and decide how ports are handled.

findings.title: update and destroy dereference a nil record for unknown ids
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id. `save_host(nil)` and `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 404. A double-clicked delete or a stale admin page triggers this. Use `find` or raise a not-found error.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation or DB index on host
findings.body: Duplicate hosts can be created, each possibly with a different category. `record_for_host` then returns an arbitrary one through `.first` with no ordering, so the category a topic is posted to is ambiguous. The migration also adds no index on `host`.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped between category and embeddable_host files
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now holds the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` holds the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. It works only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory. The contents are in the wrong files, so the diff looks like deleted category fabricators and the files are misleading to maintain.

findings.title: Test 'false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests that
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for embeddable hosts. This test passes only because `embed_truncate` is false and the topic has no embed. The test name claims a behaviour that no longer exists, so it should be removed or renamed.

findings.title: New admin controllers have no functional tests
findings.body: The specs for both new admin controllers only assert the class hierarchy. Nothing covers create, update, destroy, validation errors, default category fallback, or permission checks, and those are the paths with the nil and error-handling bugs above.
